I'm 64 this year, been farming these fields for 40 years. My father taught me, and now my two sons help when they can, but they both work in the county town factory most of the year. Between my wife, my daughter-in-law, and me, we handle the farm work. We have 16.9 mu total — not a big operation, but enough to keep us busy and fed. About 13 mu I do wheat-maize double crop. That's our foundation. The other 4 mu I keep in cotton. I've thought about giving up the cotton — at my age, the picking wears me out — but the price has been decent, and my wife is still quick with her hands.

The wheat is already in the ground, planted back in mid-October. I used about 30 jin of seed per mu — half saved from last year, half bought from the seed station to make sure I had good germination. Before planting I had the field rotavated and put down about 50 kg per mu of compound fertilizer, the 18-22-5 blend I always get from the co-op. The extension fellow told me last year I could probably cut back to 40 kg, but I've been doing this for four decades and I know my land. It doesn't have the black soil it used to. In a couple weeks when the wheat greens up and starts jointing, I'll topdress with urea — about 15 kg per mu. If it looks yellow, maybe a touch more.

I'll irrigate the wheat four times this year: green-up, jointing, heading, and grain-filling. Pumping from the well isn't free — electricity has gone up — but you can't skip water on wheat here. Four times is what I've always done, and I usually get around 450 kg per mu if the weather doesn't turn on us. I'll spray for weeds and aphids two or three times. The aphids always come in May.

For cotton, I'll plant in late April. I use plastic film — about 3.5 kg per mu — to keep the soil warm and hold moisture. I bought 2 jin of improved seed per mu. I put down compound fertilizer as basal, about 45 kg per mu, and I'll topdress with urea once in July when the bolls are setting. Cotton should give me about 300 kg per mu of seed cotton if the bollworms don't get bad. I irrigate twice — once right after planting to help it establish, and once in mid-summer. The real problem with cotton is the labor. At my age, the pruning, topping, and especially the picking in autumn — it's back-breaking. My wife and daughter-in-law help, but I may need to hire a few days of picking labor in September and October when the bolls all open at once.

After wheat harvest in early June, I have maybe five or six days to get the maize in. No time for tillage — I plant no-till with the machine right into the stubble. I buy hybrid seed, about one package per mu, costs around 50 yuan now. I put compound fertilizer down with the planter, about 50 kg per mu of the 28-6-6 type. Maize is simpler than the other crops. Two irrigations — one after planting if the rain doesn't come, and one at tasseling in August. I spray for weeds and the corn borer. Last year I got about 500 kg per mu. I'll hope for the same, though fertilizer prices are up again.

Money is always the constraint. I figure total inputs for the year — seed, fertilizer, fuel for the pump, pesticide, machine costs, and a bit of hired picking labor — will run me about 10,800 yuan. My sons send some money back from the factory, but I don't like relying on that. The wheat and maize give us grain security and steady cash. Cotton pays better per mu but the labor cost is my own aching back. At 64, I don't change much from year to year. What worked before, I do again.
